constitution.title: 대한민국헌법 (Constitution of the Republic of Korea), wholly amended 29 October 1987, Korean and English
constitution.publisher: Korea Legislation Research Institute (KLRI), Statutes of the Republic of Korea
constitution.note: Arts. 41 and 42 (National Assembly of at least 200, four-year term), 67, 68, and 70 (direct presidential election, 70 to 40 days before the term ends, single five-year term), 72 and 130 (referendums), and 118 (local councils). law.go.kr was down for maintenance on 2026-11-13; KLRI's bilingual page reproduces the official Korean text.

poea.title: 공직선거법 (Public Official Election Act), as amended to Act No. 20370 of 8 March 2024, Korean and English
poea.publisher: Korea Legislation Research Institute (KLRI), Statutes of the Republic of Korea
poea.note: Arts. 14, 21 (254 constituency and 46 proportional members), 22 and 23 (sido and sigungu council seats, proportional seats a tenth of constituency seats), and 26 (two- to four-member sigungu council districts); the English page also carries the current Arts. 34 and 35 (by-elections on the first Wednesday of April since the amendment of 29 December 2020).

poea2020.title: 공직선거법 (Public Official Election Act), as amended to Act No. 17127 of 25 March 2020, Korean and English
poea2020.publisher: Korea Legislation Research Institute (KLRI), Statutes of the Republic of Korea
poea2020.note: Arts. 34 (election days), 35, 36, 187 to 189 (plurality, no runoff; 3 percent or 5 seats for proportional seats), 190-2 (local proportional seats, 5 percent), and 200 (by-elections for constituency seats and heads, succession for proportional seats).

leaa.title: 지방교육자치에 관한 법률 (Local Education Autonomy Act), as amended to Act No. 10866 of 21 July 2011, Korean and English
leaa.publisher: Korea Legislation Research Institute (KLRI), Statutes of the Republic of Korea
leaa.note: Arts. 21 (four-year term, three consecutive terms), 43 (superintendent elected by residents, added 26 February 2010), 44, and 49; the addenda of Act No. 10046 (2010) elect education council members once with the 2010 local elections, for 2010 to 2014 only.

jeju_act.title: 제주특별자치도 설치 및 국제자유도시 조성을 위한 특별법 (Special Act on Jeju Special Self-Governing Province), as amended to Act No. 20626 of 31 December 2024

classes.note: The Constituent Assembly elected the first president in 1948 and the Assembly elected Yun Po-sun in 1960; under the Yushin constitution the National Conference for Unification elected the president in 1972, 1978, 1979, and 1980, and an electoral college of 5,278 chose Chun Doo-hwan in 1981.

classes.note: The Assembly elected the vice president in 1948 and again on 16 May 1951 after Yi Si-yeong resigned; the people elected one in 1952, 1956, and 1960, on a separate ballot from the president. The office was abolished with the constitution of 15 June 1960.

classes.name: 국민투표

classes.note: Constitutional amendments go to a referendum within 30 days of the Assembly's two-thirds vote and pass with a majority of votes cast by a majority of the electorate (Constitution Art. 130); the president may also put important policy to a vote (Art. 72). classes.name: 지방선거 재선거·보궐선거
classes.name_en: Local by-elections and re-elections (heads and council constituency seats)
classes.note: Vacant heads and council constituency seats at both tiers are filled at the annual April by-election (heads also in October); proportional vacancies pass down the list (POEA Arts. 35 and 200). Superintendent by-elections are the class superintendent.
classes.locator: https://elaw.klri.re.kr/eng_service/lawViewContent.do?hseq=64713 (Art. 35(2)1 as amended 29 December 2020: special elections and re-elections once a year on the first Wednesday of April; heads of local governments also in October)

cadence.vacancy_rule: Council seats, and heads whose cause became definite from September to February, on the first Wednesday of April; heads whose cause became definite from March to August on the first Wednesday of October, moved by Art. 34(2) when a holiday is beside it.

classes.name: 주민투표
classes.name_en: Residents' votes (local referendums)
classes.note: Residents' Voting Act (2004): local matters put to residents by the head of a sido or sigungu, on the council's or residents' request, and national-policy votes requested by a central ministry (Art. 8), run by the election commissions. The Act's text was not read (law.go.kr down); the votes held are not enumerated here.

classes.name: 주민소환투표
classes.name_en: Recall votes against local heads and council members
classes.note: Act on Residents' Recall (2006): residents may petition to recall a head or a constituency council member (not proportional members), and the vote is valid with a third of electors voting. The Act's text was not read (law.go.kr down); the votes held are not enumerated here.

classes.name: 정당 경선
classes.name_en: Party primaries and nomination contests
classes.disposition_reason: Parties run their own nomination contests; election commissions only manage the ballot when a party entrusts them (POEA Art. 57-4), and the results are the party's, not official returns.

classes.name: 전국동시조합장선거
classes.name_en: Nationwide simultaneous elections of cooperative heads
classes.disposition_reason: Heads of agricultural, fisheries, and forestry cooperatives (2015, 2019, and 2023) are chosen by members of private bodies; the election commissions run them under the Act on Entrustment of Elections for Public Organizations, but they elect no public office.

classes.name: 학교운영위원 선거인단 선거 (교육위원·교육감)
classes.name_en: Education committee members and superintendents chosen by school steering committee members (to 2006)
classes.disposition_reason: Electorates of school steering committee members (and earlier, local councils) chose education committee members and superintendents before direct election; the electorates were a few thousand appointed or school-elected members and the returns are administrative records, not public elections.

classes.name: 이장·통장 선출
classes.name_en: Village and neighborhood heads (ijang and tongjang)
classes.disposition_reason: Ri and tong heads are appointed by the eup, myeon, or dong head, sometimes after a village meeting picks a nominee; no election commission runs or publishes these choices.
